title: Peter Village: Early Woodland Enclosure in Fayette County
summary: In Fayette County, Peter Village is a large Early Woodland ditch-and-embankment enclosure, with pottery there dated to about 409–68 BCE.
bodyMarkdown:
In Fayette County lies a large Early Woodland ditch-and-embankment enclosure. Peter Village (site 15Fa166) is one of the enclosures and mounds built by the region's early Woodland peoples. Its builders left no written name for the place.

Pottery from Peter Village, dated to about 409–68 BCE, shows thick Adena wares giving way to thinner Hopewell-style types.

Ephraim Squier and Edwin Davis published a plan of Peter Village in their 1848 survey, *Ancient Monuments of the Mississippi Valley*.

Peter Village and other Bluegrass earthworks show that people of the [Adena culture](https://grokipedia.com/page/Adena_culture) and their predecessors shaped the Bluegrass into a landscape of gathering places many centuries before Kentucky's forts and stations. Adena is an archaeologists' name for a shared way of life, not the name of a single tribe.
Source: [Adena culture (Grokipedia)](https://grokipedia.com/page/Adena_culture)
